title: Bug: Create buttons do nothing — contacts, accounts, deals, tickets all broken
description:
All "Add" / "Create" buttons across the app are non-functional. The create dialog/form appears, required fields can be filled in, but clicking "Create" does nothing — no API call, no error, no feedback.

Affects: Contacts, Accounts, Deals, Tickets (all entity create flows)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Navigate to any list page (e.g. Contacts)
2. Click "+ Add Contact"
3. Fill in required fields (first name, last name, email)
4. Click "Create"
5. Nothing happens — dialog stays open, no record created

Debug checklist:

**Frontend (Freya):**
- Check browser console for errors on Create button click
- Verify the mutation hook (useCreateContact etc.) is wired to the form's onSubmit
- Check if form validation is silently failing (Zod/React Hook Form errors not displayed)
- Check if the API client base URL is correct (should be /api/v1 after the localhost fix)
- Verify the POST request is actually being sent (Network tab)

**Backend (Tyr):**
- If the POST reaches the API, check for 401/403 (JWT/org_id issues — same root cause as OMN-388)
- Check if the org_id from the JWT matches what the create handler expects
- Verify POST /api/v1/contacts returns proper response (201 + body)

This is likely related to OMN-388 (org_id mismatch) — if the API rejects creates because of org_id, the frontend may be silently swallowing the error.

Priority: CRITICAL — the app is completely unusable without create functionality.

title: Bug: FTS search response format mismatch — frontend expects grouped results
description:
## Bug Report

**Discovered in**: QA testing of OMN-238/OMN-239 (OMN-244)
**Severity**: Critical
**Branch**: `feature/OMN-238-global-search-fts`

### Issue

The global FTS search handler returns a flat array of results, but the frontend expects results grouped by entity type. This causes the search feature to always show "No results found" even when results exist.

**Backend returns** (`api/internal/handler/search.go:48-51`):
```json
{
  "results": [{"type": "ticket", ...}, {"type": "contact", ...}],
  "total": 2
}
```

**Frontend expects** (`web/src/api/types.ts:359-365`):
```json
{
  "contacts": [...],
  "accounts": [...],
  "deals": [...],
  "tickets": [...],
  "total": 2
}
```

### Impact

- `SearchPage.tsx` reads `undefined` for all entity arrays
- `totalResults` always 0
- User sees "No results found"

### Root Cause

FTS refactor changed handler to use `SearchRepository` (flat array) but forgot to add grouping logic.

### Fix

Add grouping logic in `api/internal/handler/search.go` after line 42:

```go
// Group results by type
grouped := make(map[string][]domain.SearchResultItem)
for _, item := range results {
    grouped[item.Type] = append(grouped[item.Type], item)
}

writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
    "contacts": grouped["contact"],
    "accounts": grouped["account"],
    "deals":    grouped["deal"],
    "tickets":  grouped["ticket"],
    "total":    total,
})
```

### Test Updates Required

`api/internal/handler/search_test.go` needs rewrite:
- Use `MockSearchRepository` instead of individual mocks
- Add ticket assertions
- Verify grouped response format

### Blocking

- OMN-238 (FTS backend)
- OMN-239 (FTS frontend)
- OMN-244 (QA acceptance)

title: QA: OMN-111 JWT auth with httpOnly cookies
description:
Validate the httpOnly cookie auth flow once [OMN-111](/OMN/issues/OMN-111) is merged to develop.

## Test checklist

### Login
- [ ] POST /auth/login with valid credentials → sets httpOnly cookie, returns user object
- [ ] POST /auth/login with invalid credentials → 401, no cookie set
- [ ] Cookie is HttpOnly (not accessible via JS in devtools)
- [ ] Cookie has SameSite=Strict or Lax

### Token refresh
- [ ] POST /auth/refresh with valid refresh cookie → rotates token, new cookie set
- [ ] POST /auth/refresh with expired/invalid cookie → 401

### Logout
- [ ] POST /auth/logout → cookies cleared (Set-Cookie with Max-Age=0)
- [ ] After logout, subsequent API requests return 401

### Protected routes
- [ ] GET /api/v1/contacts without cookie → 401
- [ ] GET /api/v1/contacts with valid cookie → 200

## Depends on
- [OMN-111](/OMN/issues/OMN-111) merged to develop
- [OMN-127](/OMN/issues/OMN-127) (frontend cookie flow) ideally merged too for E2E

title: P0.4 frontend: Update auth client to httpOnly cookie flow
description:
Frontend complement to OMN-111 (backend JWT/cookie auth).

**Depends on:** OMN-111 completing first.

## What to do
- Remove all `localStorage.getItem("token")` / `localStorage.setItem("token")` usage from the frontend
- Update the API client (`web/src/api/`) so it sends requests with `credentials: "include"` (cookies auto-sent)
- Remove Authorization header injection from requests — backend now reads from httpOnly cookie
- Update `/auth/login` handler: POST credentials, no token returned to JS — cookie is set by backend
- Update `/auth/logout` to POST to `/auth/logout` endpoint (clears the cookie server-side)
- Handle 401 responses: redirect to login page
- Update `/auth/refresh` if client-side token refresh logic exists

## Exit criteria
- No auth token stored in JS/localStorage anywhere
- All API calls succeed with cookie-based auth
- Login flow works end-to-end
- Logout clears the cookie
- Frontend build passes: `npm run build`

title: User onboarding for new database still not done.
CRITICAL: UserRepository incomplete — backend unbuildable
description:
## Issue

`internal/handler/setup_test.go` fails to compile:

```
internal/handler/setup_test.go:52:33: *mocks.MockUserRepository does not implement repository.UserRepository (missing method FindByEmail)
```

## Root Cause

`internal/testutil/mocks/users.go` only implements:
- `CountAll`
- `Create`

But `repository.UserRepository` interface (in `internal/repository/interfaces.go:67`) also requires:
- `FindByEmail(ctx context.Context, email string) (*domain.User, string, error)`

The actual Postgres implementation at `internal/repository/postgres/users.go:48-68` has this method.

## Fix

Add the missing method to `MockUserRepository`:

```go
func (m *MockUserRepository) FindByEmail(ctx context.Context, email string) (*domain.User, string, error) {
	args := m.Called(ctx, email)
	if args.Get(0) == nil {
		return nil, "", args.Error(2)
	}
	return args.Get(0).(*domain.User), args.String(1), args.Error(2)
}
```

## Impact

`go test ./internal/handler/...` currently fails to build, blocking all handler tests.

title: QA: OMN-53 Fix setup API response formats (snake_case vs camelCase)
description:
## What was implemented

Fixed three API contract mismatches in `omnir-go-backend/internal/handler/setup.go` (commit `c4a940f` on `develop`).

## What to test

### 1. GET /api/setup/status
- Response key must be `setupRequired` (camelCase), not `setup_required`
- `{ "setupRequired": true }` when no users exist
- `{ "setupRequired": false }` after setup is complete

### 2. POST /api/setup — request
- Send `{ "adminName": "Alice", "companyName": "Acme", "email": "alice@example.com", "password": "password123" }`
- Should succeed (201)
- Sending `{ "name": "Alice", ... }` (old format) should fail with 422 `adminName is required`

### 3. POST /api/setup — response
- Response must contain `access_token` and `refresh_token` fields
- No `token` field in response
- Both tokens should be valid JWTs
- `access_token` TTL: 24h, `refresh_token` TTL: 7 days

### 4. 409 guard
- A second POST /api/setup call should still return 409 `setup already completed`

## Known edge cases
- `companyName` is accepted but not currently persisted (no company model yet) — verify it does not cause an error
- Refresh token uses same claims as access token (no separate refresh token table yet)

### 1. Getting Started → white screen crash
Clicking "Getting Started" (or navigating to the onboarding flow) crashes to a blank white page. No error toast, no fallback UI.

### 2. Org setup re-triggers on every refresh
After the crash, refreshing the page starts the org setup wizard again from scratch — indicating onboarding completion state is not being saved server-side (or the check is failing).

### 3. Org setup changes do not persist
Completing the org setup wizard does not appear to update anything in the app — org name, logo, or other configured values are not reflected after finishing.

## Investigation notes
- Check `GET /onboarding` and `PATCH /onboarding` endpoints — likely the completion flag is not being written or the frontend is not calling the completion endpoint
- Check if the white screen has a JS error (likely an unguarded null access similar to the dashboard crash)
- The onboarding state check in AppShell fires on every load — if the backend always returns `completed: false`, the wizard re-triggers every time

## Acceptance Criteria
- Getting Started flow renders without crashing
- Completing the wizard marks onboarding as done server-side
- Wizard does not re-appear after completion
- Org setup values (name, logo, etc.) are persisted and reflected in the app

title: Frontend: SSO login buttons + TOTP 2FA enrollment + TOTP verification screens
description:
Implement the three SSO/2FA frontend flows per UX spec in OMN-485.

## Source of Truth
UX spec comment on OMN-485 (Skadi, approved by Völundr 2026-03-21). Reproduce all layouts, states, and edge cases exactly.

## Scope

### 1. Login Page — SSO buttons (LoginPage.tsx)
- Extend existing card (do NOT create new page)
- Add 'or' divider (lines + centered text, border-t border-slate-200)
- Add 'Sign in with Microsoft' and 'Sign in with Google' buttons (variant=outline, full-width, stacked, Microsoft first)
- Inline SVG icons (Microsoft M logo, Google G logo, 18x18)
- Redirecting state: spinner inline, button label changes to 'Redirecting...', both buttons disabled
- Error banners (reuse AlertCircle pattern): account_not_in_org / sso_disabled / generic_oidc_failure
- On click: navigate to /auth/sso/microsoft or /auth/sso/google (backend handles OIDC redirect)

### 2. TOTP Enrollment — /settings/security/2fa/enroll
- 3-step inline flow (no page navigation between steps)
- New StepIndicator component: numbered circles + connecting line, aria-current=step on active
- Step 1: QR code image from backend, loading spinner, 'Can't scan?' accordion with Base32 secret + copy button
- Step 2: OtpInput (new component — single Input, numeric filter, auto-submit on 6th digit). Inline error on wrong code.
- Step 3: 8 backup codes in 2-column grid. 'Copy codes' + 'Download .txt' buttons. Checkbox required before 'Done' enables.
- On 'Done': redirect to Security settings with success toast 'Two-factor authentication enabled'
- Security settings entry point: 'Set up two-factor authentication' link (or 'Manage 2FA' if already enrolled)

### 3. TOTP Verification — /login/2fa
- Same centered card as LoginPage
- OtpInput auto-focused, auto-submit on 6th digit
- 'Verify' full-width button
- Inline error on wrong code; input cleared + refocused
- Rate limit (5+ failures): role=alert banner + aria-live=polite countdown (30s), button disabled
- 'Use a backup code instead' toggle — state toggle within component, NOT a new route. Backup input: placeholder=xxxx-xxxx, autocomplete=off. Link toggles to 'Use authenticator code instead'.
- Edge: direct navigation to /login/2fa with no pending auth -> redirect to /login

## New Components to Create
- OtpInput — numeric, inputmode=numeric, autocomplete=one-time-code, maxlength=6, auto-submit callback
- StepIndicator — numbered circles + connecting line, aria-current support

## Accessibility Requirements
- SSO buttons: aria-label='Sign in with Microsoft' / aria-label='Sign in with Google'
- OTP input: aria-label='One-time code', inputmode=numeric, autocomplete=one-time-code, maxlength=6
- Backup code input: aria-label='Backup code', autocomplete=off
- Progress steps: ol role=list with aria-current=step
- QR image: alt='TOTP QR code — scan with your authenticator app'
- All error messages: role=alert
- Rate-limit countdown: aria-live=polite
- Full keyboard nav; focus moves to new step heading on step transition

## API Endpoints Expected from Backend (Tyr)
- GET /api/auth/totp/setup — returns { qr_url, secret } for enrollment Step 1
- POST /api/auth/totp/verify-setup — { code } validates and activates TOTP
- GET /api/auth/totp/backup-codes — returns 8 backup codes (only shown at enrollment)
- POST /api/auth/totp/verify — { code } validates at login, returns session cookie or error
- GET /auth/sso/microsoft, GET /auth/sso/google — triggers OIDC redirect
- GET /auth/callback — OIDC code exchange (backend; frontend just navigates to error or success)

If these endpoints don't exist yet, stub them with mock responses and note in your PR.

## Definition of Done
- All three flows render and function correctly
- All states (loading, error, success) handled
- All edge cases from the UX spec handled
- OtpInput and StepIndicator unit tested (Vitest)
- Full TypeScript (no any)
- No lint errors
- PR description links to OMN-485 spec comment

title: Phase 12: SSO — OIDC login backend (Google Workspace + generic OIDC) + TOTP 2FA
description:
## Objective

Add OIDC-based SSO and TOTP 2FA to Omnir. Unlocks enterprise sales. SAML behind a feature flag (deferred).

## Scope

### OIDC Login
- Use `coreos/go-oidc/v3` + `golang.org/x/oauth2`
- Support: Google Workspace (well-known config) + generic OIDC provider (Okta, Entra ID via config)
- Org-level SSO config table:
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE sso_configs (
      id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      org_id          UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES orgs(id),
      provider        TEXT NOT NULL,       -- google | oidc
      client_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
      client_secret   TEXT NOT NULL,       -- encrypted at rest
      issuer_url      TEXT NOT NULL,
      attribute_mapping JSONB,             -- map OIDC claims → role
      enabled         BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  );
  ```
- Flow: `GET /auth/sso/{orgSlug}/login` → OIDC redirect → `GET /auth/sso/callback` → issue JWT
- Provision user on first login if not exists (JIT provisioning)
- Role mapping: OIDC claim (e.g. `groups`) → Omnir role via `attribute_mapping` JSONB config

### TOTP 2FA
- Library: `pquerna/otp`
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/2fa/setup` — generate TOTP secret, return `otpauth://` URI + QR data URL
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/2fa/verify` — verify TOTP code, activate 2FA, return 8 backup codes (bcrypt-hashed, stored in `totp_backup_codes` table)
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/2fa/disable` — disable (requires password confirmation)
- Auth flow update: after JWT, if 2FA enabled → return `requires_2fa: true` in login response → frontend prompts TOTP → `POST /api/v1/auth/2fa/verify` → issue full JWT

### Org Policy
- `orgs` table: add `require_2fa BOOL DEFAULT false`, `sso_required BOOL DEFAULT false`
- If `sso_required`, reject password login for that org

### Security
- OIDC client secrets encrypted at rest (use app-level AES-256 encryption, key from `SSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env)
- Backup codes: single-use, bcrypt-hashed
- TOTP window: ±1 interval (30s tolerance)

## Owner
Tyr (backend). Freya consumes in OMN-442. Heimdall provisions env vars in OMN-443.

### Slack Integration
```sql
CREATE TABLE slack_connections (

  org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) UNIQUE,
  team_id TEXT NOT NULL,
```

title: Phase 13 / Email: Advanced inbox integration backend (Gmail/Outlook OAuth sync, reply tracking, template library)
description:
## Context

Phase 13 Area 1 (backend). Email integration turns Omnir into a daily-driver communication hub — users never need to leave the CRM to see their inbox thread with a contact.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE email_connections (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  provider TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (provider IN ('gmail', 'outlook')),
  access_token_enc TEXT NOT NULL,
  refresh_token_enc TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_expiry TIMESTAMPTZ,
  email_address TEXT NOT NULL,
  sync_cursor TEXT,
  last_synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(user_id, provider)
);

CREATE TABLE email_templates (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  created_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject_template TEXT NOT NULL,
  body_html_template TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

## Scope

1. **OAuth flows** — Gmail (Google APIs OAuth2) + Outlook (Microsoft Graph OAuth) connect/disconnect endpoints; store tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM using `SSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
2. **Background sync worker** — poll each connected inbox every 5min; match emails to contacts by from/to address; thread via In-Reply-To + References headers; store in existing `emails` table (`direction=inbound`, `source=inbox`)
3. **Reply tracking** — detect contact replies to outbound emails via In-Reply-To matching; update `emails.replied_at` on original sent email
4. **Email template library** — full CRUD under `/api/v1/email-templates`; server-side mustache-style variable substitution (`{{contact.first_name}}`, `{{sender.name}}`, `{{deal.title}}`); preview endpoint renders with sample data

## API Endpoints

- `GET /api/v1/integrations/email/status` — list connected providers per current user
- `GET /api/v1/integrations/gmail/auth` — initiates OAuth redirect
- `GET /api/v1/integrations/gmail/callback` — handles OAuth callback, encrypts + stores token
- `DELETE /api/v1/integrations/gmail/disconnect` — revokes token + deletes connection
- Same paths for `/outlook`
- `GET/POST /api/v1/email-templates`
- `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/email-templates/:id`
- `POST /api/v1/email-templates/:id/preview`

## Acceptance Criteria

- User can connect Gmail or Outlook via OAuth (browser redirect flow)
- Emails from that inbox sync to `emails` table linked to matching contacts by address
- Reply detection sets `replied_at` on original outbound email
- Admins can create/edit/delete email templates with variable placeholders
- Preview endpoint renders template with sample contact/sender/deal data
- OAuth tokens encrypted at rest, never returned in API responses
- QA subtask created when done

title: Phase 2 / Backend: Org signup + ORG_MODE env var routing
description:
Org signup endpoint and ORG_MODE routing.

Endpoint: POST /api/v1/auth/signup
- Body: {orgName, adminName, email, password}
- TX: INSERT INTO orgs (name, slug), INSERT INTO users (org_id, email, ...)

ORG_MODE routing in config:

title: Phase 12: Mobile PWA — service worker, offline mode, mobile-optimized UI
description:
## Objective

Implement a Progressive Web App (PWA) for Omnir CRM. This is the most-requested capability gap, explicitly deferred from Phase 10.

## Scope

**Freya owns frontend implementation:**

### Service Worker + App Manifest
- Add `manifest.webmanifest` (name, icons, display: standalone, theme color)
- Register a Workbox-based service worker for precaching and runtime caching
- Handle install prompt (A2HS) for iOS and Android
- Configure Vite PWA plugin (`vite-plugin-pwa`)

### Offline Mode
- Offline read mode for: tickets list, contacts list, deals pipeline, ticket detail, contact detail
- Cache last-fetched data in IndexedDB via TanStack Query persistence adapter
- Offline indicator in UI (banner when `navigator.onLine === false`)
- Queue write mutations while offline; sync on reconnect (Background Sync API where supported, fallback: sync on tab focus)

### Mobile-Optimized Layouts
- Bottom tab navigation (replacing sidebar for mobile viewport)
- Touch-friendly list rows (min 44px touch targets)
- Swipe-to-action on list items (mark resolved, assign)
- Responsive ticket detail: full-screen on mobile, slide-in comment panel
- Responsive deal Kanban: horizontal scroll on mobile

### Push Notifications
- Web Push via VAPID (coordinate with Tyr for push subscription endpoint)
- Notification types: ticket assigned, ticket updated, deal stage changed

## Key Decisions
- No React Native — PWA avoids a second codebase
- Offline writes: IndexedDB queue + Background Sync
- Saga owns mobile UX design (coordinate designs before implementation)

## Owner
Freya (frontend). Coordinate with Saga (UX) and Tyr (push subscription API).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] App installable on Android Chrome and iOS Safari
- [ ] Tickets and contacts readable offline
- [ ] Mutations queued and replayed on reconnect
- [ ] Lighthouse PWA score ≥ 90
- [ ] Mobile layouts pass Saga UX review

## User Story

As a **super-admin**, I want to switch between tenant orgs in the UI so that I can inspect, debug, and support any org in the system without leaving the app.

## Context

Phase 2 backend work is in progress (OMN-433: RLS policies, OMN-434: org signup + ORG_MODE routing). The rewrite plan requires a frontend tenant switcher as the final Phase 2 deliverable.

The backend exposes the necessary org-scope context via JWT (org_id claim) and the middleware sets app.current_org_id per request. The frontend needs a UI mechanism for super-admins to:
1. See the list of all orgs in the system
2. Switch the active org context (re-issue a scoped JWT or pass X-Org-ID header)
3. Display a persistent banner when operating in a non-default org

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Org switcher dropdown** appears in the top navigation bar for users with role=admin and ORG_MODE=multi; hidden in single-tenant mode.
2. **Org list** is fetched from GET /api/v1/admin/orgs (super-admin only endpoint) and displayed with org name + slug.

4. **Active org banner** — when operating in a non-primary org, a dismissable warning banner is shown (e.g. "Viewing as: Acme Corp").
5. **Exit criteria** matches the plan: two orgs in the same DB cannot see each other data — manual smoke test verifies this end-to-end via the switcher.

title: Phase 2: Multi-tenancy hardening — RLS, org signup, ORG_MODE=multi
description:
## Phase 2 — Multi-tenancy Hardening

From `plans/praestos-rewrite-plan.md`.

## Scope

### 1. RLS policies
- Enable row-level security on all domain tables (tickets, contacts, accounts, leads, ticket_comments, ticket_attachments)
- Policy: `USING (org_id = current_setting('app.current_org_id')::uuid)`
- Integration test: two orgs in same DB cannot see each other's data under any query path
- Go middleware must call `SET LOCAL app.current_org_id = $1` on every request

### 2. Org signup flow
- `POST /auth/signup` — create org + admin user atomically
- Slug generation from org name (unique, URL-safe)
- Seed default admin user
- Support `ORG_MODE=single` (skip signup, single pre-seeded org) vs `ORG_MODE=multi` (signup enabled)

### 3. ORG_MODE=multi support
- Env var `ORG_MODE` controls behaviour
- In multi mode: enforce RLS, enable signup endpoint, expose org slug in JWT claims
- In single mode: bypass RLS (or set org_id from env), disable signup route

## Exit criteria
- Two orgs in same DB cannot see each other's data under any query path
- `POST /auth/signup` creates a new isolated org
- All existing tests pass in both `ORG_MODE=single` and `ORG_MODE=multi`

## Notes
- See section 3 of praestos-rewrite-plan.md for RLS SQL and middleware pattern
- No frontend tenant-switcher required in Phase 2 (internal super-admin only, can defer to Phase 3)

title: Phase 1b: Contact/Account sidebar panel on ticket detail
description:
## Context

This is the final undelivered item from Phase 1b of the PraestOS spec (praestos-rewrite-plan.md).

## Spec requirement

> Contact/Account linked to tickets (sidebar relationship panel)
> Exit criteria: ticket contact panel resolves live

## What this means

On the ticket detail page, there should be a sidebar (or relationship panel) that:
- Shows the linked contact (name, email, phone) if set on the ticket
- Shows the linked account if the contact has one
- Allows updating the linked contact/account inline

## Why it matters

This is the Phase 1b exit criterion. Without it, the Help Desk and CRM modules are not properly integrated. Agents cannot see who submitted a ticket without leaving the ticket view.

## Notes
- Ticket schema already has contact_id and account_id columns
- Backend query needs to JOIN and return contact/account data on GET /tickets/:id
- Frontend needs a sidebar component on TicketDetail

title: QA: Phase 1b / Contact sidebar panel on TicketDetail (OMN-426)
description:
Acceptance QA for the contact/account sidebar panel on the ticket detail view (OMN-426 + OMN-427 + OMN-428). Activate once PRs are merged to develop.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **View** — Ticket with a linked contact shows contact name, email, phone, and account name (if set) in the sidebar panel
2. **Empty state** — Ticket with no contact shows "No contact linked" + "+ Link contact" button
3. **Link flow** — Typing in the search input triggers GET /api/v1/contacts?q= after 300ms debounce; results dropdown shows up to 10 contacts with name + account subtitle
4. **Select** — Selecting a contact optimistically shows the card; PATCH /api/v1/tickets/:id/contact fires in background; confirmed on success
5. **Unlink** — Clicking × removes the card optimistically; backend call fires; reverts on error with inline error message
6. **Change** — Clicking ↔ replaces card with inline search; Escape cancels and restores previous card
7. **Error handling** — On API failure, optimistic update reverts and inline red error text appears (auto-dismisses after 4s)
8. **No regression** — Existing ticket fields (subject, status, priority, assignee, comments) render correctly
9. **Org isolation** — Contact search only returns contacts belonging to the current org

## Reference
- UX spec: [OMN-430](/OMN/issues/OMN-430)
- Backend PR: see [OMN-427](/OMN/issues/OMN-427)
- Frontend PR: see [OMN-428](/OMN/issues/OMN-428)

title: Email Sequences: tracking pixel, click redirect, bounce webhook, unsubscribe endpoint
description: ## Context The sequence worker (`worker/sequence_worker.go`) sends emails via `mailer.SendDirect()` with no tracking token injection. The handler (`handler/sequences.go`) has no routes for tracking or unsubscribe. These four endpoints are required for OMN-380 QA to pass. ## Required Endpoints ### 1. Open tracking pixel - `GET /track/open/{token}` — returns a 1×1 transparent PNG, records `opened` event - Sequence worker must inject `` in outbound email HTML body - Token encodes: enrollment_id, step_id, org_id (JWT or HMAC-signed) ### 2. Click tracking redirect - `GET /track/click/{token}?url={destination}` — records `clicked` event, 302 redirects to `url` - Sequence worker must rewrite all `` in email HTML to `/track/click/{token}?url={original}` ### 3. Unsubscribe endpoint - `GET /unsubscribe/{token}` — one-click: sets enrollment status to `unsubscribed`, sets contact opt_out=true, returns confirmation HTML page - `POST /unsubscribe/{token}` — same action (for clients that POST the unsubscribe form) - Sequence worker must inject `Unsubscribe` in every outbound email - **Legally required (CAN-SPAM Act)** ### 4. Bounce webhook - `POST /api/emails/bounce` — compatible with SendGrid/Mailgun bounce webhook format - On bounce: record `bounced` event, set enrollment status to `bounced`, update contact bounce_count - Auth via webhook secret header (reuse existing pattern from inbound email) ## Token Format Use HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens (base64url-encoded). Fields: org_id, sequence_id, enrollment_id, step_id. Include expiry (90 days). Store secret in env var `SEQUENCE_TOKEN_SECRET`. ## Routing In `main.go`: ```go // Public (no auth required) r.Get("/track/open/{token}", trackingHandler.OpenPixel) r.Get("/track/click/{token}", trackingHandler.ClickRedirect) r.Get("/unsubscribe/{token}", trackingHandler.Unsubscribe) r.Post("/unsubscribe/{token}", trackingHandler.Unsubscribe) // Authenticated r.Post("/api/emails/bounce", emailHandler.HandleBounce) ``` ## Worker Changes `processEnrollment` must: 1. Generate open/click/unsubscribe tokens for each email step 2. Call `mailer.SendSequenceEmail(to, subject, htmlBody, tokens)` that injects pixel, rewrites links, appends unsubscribe footer ## Acceptance Criteria - Open pixel fires `opened` event in sequence_events - Click redirect records `clicked` event, forwards to original URL - Unsubscribe sets enrollment=unsubscribed AND contact opt_out=true - Bounce webhook records `bounced` event, sets enrollment=bounced - OMN-380 can proceed with full QA checklist When done: create QA subtask, comment on OMN-380 to unblock Skadi.

title: Phase 10 / Documents: Fix soft delete + MIME allowlist (OMN-372 gaps)
description:
## Context

Skadi QA review (OMN-374) found two spec gaps in the OMN-372 attachment implementation that must be fixed before QA sign-off.

## Required Fixes

### 1. Soft delete (not hard delete)

Current: handler uses `DELETE FROM attachments WHERE id = $1` — physically removes the row.

Required: add `deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column to `attachments` table and use `UPDATE attachments SET deleted_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1`. All `GET` queries must filter `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.

- Migration: add `deleted_at` column to `attachments` table
- Handler: change DELETE endpoint to soft delete
- List handler: add `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` filter

### 2. MIME type allowlist

Current: handler detects content type but does not validate against an allowlist.

Required: reject disallowed MIME types with 415 Unsupported Media Type.

Default allowlist (env-configurable via `ATTACHMENT_ALLOWED_MIMES`):
```
image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp,
application/pdf,
application/msword, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document,
application/vnd.ms-excel, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet,
text/plain, text/csv
```

Return `{"error": "file type not allowed", "mime_type": "<detected>"}` on rejection.

## Not in scope (deferred)
- S3/MinIO migration — tracked separately, local FS is acceptable for Phase 10
- Presigned URL expiry — deferred with local FS

## Done when
- `attachments` table has `deleted_at` column
- DELETE endpoint sets `deleted_at` instead of hard-deleting
- GET lists filter `deleted_at IS NULL`
- Upload endpoint rejects disallowed MIME types with 415
- Skadi can verify soft delete and MIME blocking in QA

title: Bug: API key scope enforcement
API Key Scope Enforcement Not Implemented (OMN-347)
description:
## Issue

API key scope enforcement is NOT implemented. The `scopes` field (`read` vs `write`) is stored in the database but never validated or enforced during authentication/authorization.

**Discovered during:** OMN-351 QA review
**Recommend assigning to:** @Tyr (backend engineer)

## Root Cause

The auth middleware (`api/internal/middleware/auth.go:64-102`) retrieves the API key and checks revocation/expiration, but **never inspects the `scopes` field**. Authorization is based solely on the key owner's user role.

### Missing Implementation

1. **Scope validation on creation** — `api/internal/handler/api_keys.go:96-99` accepts any string in scopes array without validation
2. **Scope enforcement on auth** — `api/internal/middleware/auth.go:95-100` constructs claims from user role only, ignores API key scopes
3. **HTTP method enforcement** — No middleware checks if API key scope allows the requested method

## Expected Behavior

### Scope Validation
- Creating key with `scopes: ["read"]` or `scopes: ["write"]` → success
- Creating key with `scopes: ["admin"]` or invalid value → 422 Unprocessable Entity

### Scope Enforcement
- `read`-scoped key + GET request → 200 (allowed)
- `read`-scoped key + POST/PATCH/DELETE request → 403 Forbidden
- `write`-scoped key + any HTTP method → 200 (allowed)

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Add Scope Validation (Handler)

In `api/internal/handler/api_keys.go:Create`:

```go
validScopes := map[string]bool{"read": true, "write": true}
for _, s := range req.Scopes {
    if !validScopes[s] {
        writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, fmt.Sprintf("invalid scope: %s", s))
        return
    }
}
```

### 2. Extend Claims to Include Scopes

In `api/internal/auth/jwt.go` (or wherever Claims is defined):

```go
type Claims struct {
    UserID       uuid.UUID `json:"user_id"`
    OrgID        uuid.UUID `json:"org_id"`
    Role         string    `json:"role"`
    APIKeyScopes []string  `json:"api_key_scopes,omitempty"` // NEW
}
```

### 3. Populate Scopes in Auth Middleware

In `api/internal/middleware/auth.go:authenticateAPIKey` (lines 95-100):

```go
claims := &auth.Claims{
    UserID:       apiKey.CreatedBy,
    OrgID:        apiKey.OrgID,
    Role:         string(user.Role),
    APIKeyScopes: apiKey.Scopes, // NEW
}
```

### 4. Create Scope Enforcement Middleware

New file: `api/internal/middleware/api_key_scope.go`

```go
func RequireAPIKeyScope(allowedMethods ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
    return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
        return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
            claims, ok := ClaimsFromContext(r)
            if !ok {
                http.Error(w, `{"error":"unauthorized"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
                return
            }
            
            // If no API key scopes, this is JWT auth — allow all methods
            if len(claims.APIKeyScopes) == 0 {
                next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
                return
            }
            
            // Check if API key has required scope
            hasWrite := false
            for _, s := range claims.APIKeyScopes {
                if s == "write" {
                    hasWrite = true
                    break
                }
            }
            
            // Read-only keys can only use GET
            if !hasWrite && r.Method != "GET" {
                http.Error(w, `{"error":"forbidden","code":"insufficient_scope"}`, http.StatusForbidden)
                return
            }
            
            next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
        })
    }
}
```

### 5. Apply Middleware to Routes

In route definitions, wrap handlers that should enforce scopes:

```go
r.With(middleware.RequireAPIKeyScope()).Post("/contacts", h.Create)
r.With(middleware.RequireAPIKeyScope()).Patch("/contacts/{id}", h.Update)
// etc.
```

Or apply globally to all routes except public endpoints.

## Testing

1. Create `read`-scoped key
2. Use key for GET request → expect 200
3. Use key for POST request → expect 403
4. Create `write`-scoped key
5. Use key for POST request → expect 200
6. Try to create key with scope `["admin"]` → expect 422

## References

- QA Report: `api/testdata/OMN-351-api-keys-qa-report.md`
- Parent Issue: OMN-347 (Phase 9 Area 2: API Keys for Integrations)
- Blocking: OMN-351 (QA review)

## Priority

**High** — This is a security feature. Without scope enforcement, the `scopes` field is cosmetic and provides no actual access control.

title: Bug: API key scope enforcement
Bug: API key scope enforcement not implemented
description:
## Bug Report

Found by Skadi QA (OMN-351).

### Problem

The scopes field on API keys is stored but never checked. Auth middleware (api/internal/middleware/auth.go:64-102) retrieves the API key but never inspects the scopes field. Any valid API key grants full access based on owner role, regardless of scope.

### Impact

- read vs write scope restrictions are non-functional
- Invalid scopes (e.g. admin) are accepted without error  
- API key security model is broken

### Fix Required

1. Enforce scope validation in auth middleware — check scopes on every request against the required scope for the endpoint
2. Validate allowed scopes on key creation (reject unknown values)

### References
- QA report: api/testdata/OMN-351-api-keys-qa-report.md
- Blocking: [OMN-351](/OMN/issues/OMN-351) (Skadi QA)

title: Bug: API key scope enforcement not implemented
description:
Found by Skadi QA ([OMN-351](/OMN/issues/OMN-351)).

**Problem:** The scopes field on API keys is stored but never checked in auth middleware (auth.go:64-102). Any valid API key grants full access based on owner role, regardless of scope configured.

**Blocking issues:**
1. read vs write scope restrictions non-functional
2. Invalid scopes (e.g. admin) accepted without error

**Fix required:**
1. Enforce scope validation in auth middleware on every request
2. Validate allowed scopes on key creation

**Reference:** api/testdata/OMN-351-api-keys-qa-report.md

title: Phase 9 Area 2: API Keys for Integrations
description:
## Context

External integrations (webhooks are already shipped in Phase 6) need a way to authenticate against the Omnir API without sharing user credentials. API keys are the standard solution.

## Task

Implement API key issuance and authentication for the Omnir CRM API.

### Backend (Tyr)

1. **Schema** — new `api_keys` table:
   - `id`, `org_id`, `created_by_user_id`, `name` (human label), `key_hash` (bcrypt), `key_prefix` (first 8 chars, for display), `scopes` (JSONB array), `last_used_at`, `expires_at` (nullable), `revoked_at` (nullable), `created_at`
   - Migration: `019_api_keys.sql`

2. **Key generation**
   - Format: `omn_<random 32 bytes base64url>` (~45 chars)
   - Store only `bcrypt(key)` — never store plaintext after creation
   - Return plaintext once at creation (never retrievable again)

3. **Auth middleware** — support `Authorization: Bearer omn_...` in addition to JWT
   - Resolve to org + user context via API key lookup
   - Reject revoked/expired keys with 401
   - Update `last_used_at` asynchronously

4. **API endpoints**
   - `POST /api/api-keys` — create (returns plaintext once)
   - `GET /api/api-keys` — list (shows prefix + metadata, never plaintext)
   - `DELETE /api/api-keys/:id` — revoke

5. **Scopes** (Phase 9 scope = read-only and full-access only; fine-grained in later phase)
   - `read` — GET endpoints only
   - `write` — all endpoints

### Frontend (Freya)

1. Settings page: `/settings/api-keys`
   - List existing keys (name, prefix, created date, last used, status)
   - Create new key — name + scope selection; show plaintext once in modal with copy button and explicit warning
   - Revoke key — confirm dialog

### Exit criteria
- Integrations can authenticate with `omn_...` bearer tokens
- Keys are admin-manageable via UI
- Plaintext never persisted or re-exposed after creation
- QA subtask created when done

title: Phase 8 / API Rate Limiting + Audit Log: backend implementation
description:
## Context

Deferred from Phase 7. Required before SaaS launch. Two concerns: rate limiting per user to prevent abuse, and an admin-visible audit trail of CRM mutations.

## Part 1: Rate Limiting

### Approach

Use an in-process sliding window rate limiter (no Redis dependency for Phase 8; Redis upgrade is Phase 9+ if needed).

### Implementation

- Middleware: `RateLimitMiddleware(limit int, window time.Duration)` applied globally in router
- Default limits:
  - Authenticated users: 300 req/min
  - Unauthenticated: 30 req/min (login/signup endpoints)
  - Write endpoints (POST/PATCH/DELETE): 60 req/min
- Headers on every response: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`
- On limit exceeded: `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` header and JSON error body
- Key: `userID` for authenticated, `IP` for unauthenticated

### Config

Limits configurable via env vars: `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH`, `RATE_LIMIT_UNAUTH`, `RATE_LIMIT_WRITE`

## Part 2: Audit Log

### Schema (new migration)

```sql
CREATE TABLE audit_log (
  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  user_id      UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  agent_id     TEXT,  -- if action was by an API client
  action       TEXT NOT NULL,  -- created | updated | deleted | converted | login | export
  entity_type  TEXT NOT NULL,  -- contact | deal | account | user | view | ...
  entity_id    UUID,
  entity_name  TEXT,  -- snapshot of name at time of action
  changes      JSONB,  -- {field: {from, to}} for updates
  ip_address   TEXT,
  user_agent   TEXT,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX ON audit_log(org_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX ON audit_log(org_id, entity_type, entity_id);
```

### Audit hooks

- Log all Create/Update/Delete operations on: contacts, accounts, deals, leads, users, saved_views
- Log login events (success + failure)
- Log data exports (CSV export endpoints)
- Capture `changes` diff for PATCH operations (before/after values)

### Admin endpoints

- `GET /api/admin/audit-log?entityType=&entityId=&userId=&action=&from=&to=&page=&limit=` — paginated, admin-only
- `GET /api/admin/audit-log/export` — CSV export of audit log (admin only)

### Access control

- Only users with `role = 'admin'` can access audit log endpoints
- Non-admins get 403

## Tests

- Rate limiter: verify 429 after limit, reset after window
- Audit log: verify entries created on CRUD operations, correct diff captured
- Admin endpoint access control

## Exit criteria

- Rate limiter active and returning correct headers
- Audit log populated for all tracked entity mutations
- Admin list/export endpoints working
- Tests passing
- QA subtask created when done

title: Phase 8 / Lead Management: backend API (scoring, source tracking, conversion)
description:
## Context

Leads are currently modeled as contacts with `stage = 'lead'`. Phase 8 formalizes lead management with scoring, source tracking, and a conversion flow.

## Technical Requirements

### Schema changes (new migration)

Add to `contacts` table (or a `lead_details` side table):
```sql
lead_score       INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
lead_source      TEXT,  -- e.g. web_form, cold_outbound, referral, import
converted_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
converted_by     UUID REFERENCES users(id),
converted_deal_id UUID REFERENCES deals(id),
```

### New endpoints

- `GET /api/leads` — list contacts where `stage = 'lead'`, supports pagination + filters (source, score range, assigned_to)
- `PATCH /api/leads/{id}/score` — update `lead_score` (accepts `delta` or absolute `score`)
- `POST /api/leads/{id}/convert` — converts lead: sets `stage = 'contact'`, creates a deal (optional body: `{createDeal: bool, dealTitle: string, pipelineId: string}`), records `converted_at/by/deal_id`
- `GET /api/leads/sources` — returns distinct lead source values for filter dropdowns

### Scoring rules

Score is manual for Phase 8 (user-driven). Automated scoring is Phase 9+.

### Soft deletes

Conversion does NOT delete the contact — it changes stage and records conversion metadata.

### Tests

Unit tests for conversion logic. Integration tests for list/filter/convert endpoints. Edge cases: double-convert (idempotent), convert with deal creation failure (rollback).

## Exit criteria

- Leads list endpoint with filtering works
- Score update endpoint works
- Conversion endpoint transitions stage and optionally creates a deal
- All endpoints covered by tests
- QA subtask created when done

title: P8.2: Lead management — backend API
description:
## Goal
Dedicated lead lifecycle with scoring, source tracking, and conversion flow (lead -> contact -> deal).

## Approach
Leads are a first-class entity (not just contacts with stage='lead'). This allows richer lead-specific metadata.

## Schema (new migration)
```sql
CREATE TABLE leads (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  first_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT,
  phone TEXT,
  company TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  source TEXT CHECK (source IN ('web','referral','cold_outreach','event','import','other')),
  score INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (score >= 0 AND score <= 100),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new' CHECK (status IN ('new','contacted','qualified','disqualified','converted')),
  owner_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  converted_contact_id UUID REFERENCES contacts(id),
  converted_deal_id UUID REFERENCES deals(id),
  converted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  notes TEXT,
  custom_fields JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);
CREATE INDEX idx_leads_org ON leads (org_id, status) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_leads_org_score ON leads (org_id, score DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
```

## API Endpoints
- `GET /api/v1/leads` — list with filters (status, source, owner_id, min_score, search, page, per_page)
- `POST /api/v1/leads` — create
- `GET /api/v1/leads/:id` — get
- `PATCH /api/v1/leads/:id` — update (score, status, owner, etc.)
- `DELETE /api/v1/leads/:id` — soft delete
- `POST /api/v1/leads/:id/convert` — convert to contact + deal

## Conversion endpoint
Body: `{ "create_deal": true, "deal_title": "...", "pipeline_id": "..." }`
Response: `{ "contact_id": "...", "deal_id": "..." }`
Sets converted_contact_id, converted_deal_id, converted_at, status='converted'

## Scoring
Score is manually set or updated via PATCH. Future: auto-scoring via rules.

title: P8.1: Saved searches + views — backend API
description:

Allow users to save filter combinations as named views, shareable across the team.

```sql
CREATE TABLE saved_views (

  org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  owner_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  entity_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (entity_type IN ('contact','account','deal','ticket')),
  filters JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_shared BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);
CREATE INDEX idx_saved_views_org ON saved_views (org_id, entity_type) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
```

## API Endpoints
- `GET /api/v1/saved-views?entity_type=contact` — list views (own + shared)
- `POST /api/v1/saved-views` — create
- `PUT /api/v1/saved-views/:id` — update (owner or admin only)
- `DELETE /api/v1/saved-views/:id` — soft delete (owner or admin only)

## Request body
```json
{ "name": "Hot leads", "entity_type": "contact", "filters": {"stage":"lead"}, "is_shared": true }
```

## Notes
- `filters` is freeform JSONB — frontend stores whatever filter state it uses
- Shared views visible to all org members (filter by org_id + is_shared OR owner_id=me)

title: Custom field values read/write on entities
description:
## Context

## Goal
Read and write custom field values stored in the existing `custom_fields JSONB` column on contacts, accounts, and deals.

- Validate incoming values against the def (type check, required check, select options membership)
- Unknown field names (not in custom_field_defs for this company+entityType) should be rejected with 422

## Notes
- Store values as `{"fieldName": value}` — no wrapper, just flat JSON
- Null means "not set" — distinguish from missing key
- Reading: always return all defined fields for the entity type (even if null in storage)

## Done when
- GET entity endpoints include `customFields` populated from defs
- PATCH accepts and validates `customFields`
- Integration tests cover: set, update, clear, invalid type, unknown field

## Context

## Goal
Backend plumbing to create, store, and deliver notifications. No UI in this ticket.

## Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE notifications (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  user_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  actor_id      UUID REFERENCES users(id),  -- who triggered it (null = system)
  kind          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN (
    'activity_reminder',
    'deal_stage_changed',
    'mention',
    'assignment'
  )),
  entity_type   TEXT,  -- 'deal', 'contact', 'activity'
  entity_id     UUID,
  title         TEXT NOT NULL,
  body          TEXT,
  read_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
  emailed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,  -- null = not yet emailed
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX ON notifications (user_id, read_at, created_at DESC);
```

## API Endpoints
- `GET /api/notifications?limit=50&before=<cursor>` — paginated, newest first, auth user only
- `GET /api/notifications/unread-count` — returns `{count: N}` for badge
- `POST /api/notifications/{id}/read` — mark one read
- `POST /api/notifications/read-all` — mark all read

## Trigger Points (internal, no separate endpoint)
Emit notifications from existing handlers:
- Deal stage change → notify deal owner
- Activity created with due_date → schedule reminder (use existing activity.due_date)
- @mention in note body → notify mentioned user (parse `@username` pattern)
- Issue/activity assigned to user → notify assignee

## Email Delivery
- Background goroutine polls `WHERE emailed_at IS NULL AND created_at < now() - interval '5 minutes'`
- Send via existing SMTP config; update `emailed_at`
- Skip email if user has no email address

## Done when
- Migration runs, all endpoints work
- Notifications fire on deal stage change + assignment
- Email delivery loop works end-to-end (test with staging SMTP)
- QA subtask created

title: Custom field definitions API
description:
## Context
Phase 7 — Area 1: Custom Fields. The `custom_fields JSONB` column already exists on contacts/accounts/deals tables. This issue covers defining the field schemas.

## Goal
Allow admins to define custom field schemas per entity type so the frontend can render them dynamically.

## Schema
New migration: `custom_field_defs` table
```sql
CREATE TABLE custom_field_defs (
  id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  entity_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (entity_type IN ('contact', 'account', 'deal')),
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,  -- machine key, snake_case
  label       TEXT NOT NULL,  -- display label
  field_type  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (field_type IN ('text', 'number', 'date', 'boolean', 'select', 'multi_select')),
  options     JSONB,          -- [{"value":"x","label":"X"}] for select types
  required    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  sort_order  INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  deleted_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  UNIQUE (company_id, entity_type, name)
);
```

## API Endpoints
- `GET /api/custom-field-defs?entityType=contact|account|deal` — list defs for company (from JWT)
- `POST /api/custom-field-defs` — create new def
- `PATCH /api/custom-field-defs/{id}` — update label, options, required, sort_order (not name or type)
- `DELETE /api/custom-field-defs/{id}` — soft delete

## Validation
- Max 50 custom fields per (company, entity_type)
- `name` must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`
- `options` required when field_type is `select` or `multi_select`

## Done when
- Migration runs cleanly
- All 4 endpoints work with proper auth
- Unit tests cover CRUD + validation edge cases
- QA subtask created

title: Fix CI: test mock gaps blocking develop branch
description:
## Context

CI has been failing on `develop` (and PR #22 / OMN-265). The failures are pre-existing mock/interface gaps that became visible after recent merges:

### Root cause

The `AccountRepository` interface gained `GetByName` in a recent merge, but `api/internal/testutil/mocks/accounts.go` was never updated. Similarly, handler constructors changed signatures but tests were not updated.

### Specific errors

```
internal/handler/accounts_test.go: *mocks.MockAccountRepository does not implement repository.AccountRepository (missing method GetByName)
internal/handler/export_test.go: *mocks.MockAccountRepository does not implement repository.AccountRepository (missing method GetByName)
internal/handler/search_test.go: too many arguments in call to handler.NewSearchHandler
    have (*mocks.MockContactRepository, *mocks.MockAccountRepository, *mocks.MockDealRepository)
    want (repository.SearchRepository)
internal/handler/tickets_email_test.go: not enough arguments in call to handler.NewTicketHandler
    have (*mocks.MockTicketRepository, *mocks.MockTicketCommentRepository, *mocks.MockTicketAttachmentRepository)
    want (repository.TicketRepository, repository.TicketCommentRepository, repository.TicketAttachmentRepository, repository.SLAPolicyRepository)
```

Also: `golangci-lint` version mismatch — go1.24 linter vs go1.25 target. This can be fixed by pinning `go` directive in `go.mod` to `go 1.24` or upgrading the CI action to use golangci-lint v2.

## Required fixes

1. Add `GetByName` method to `MockAccountRepository` in `api/internal/testutil/mocks/accounts.go`
2. Fix `search_test.go` — `NewSearchHandler` now takes a `SearchRepository`, not three separate repos
3. Fix `tickets_email_test.go` — `NewTicketHandler` now requires 4 args (add `MockSLAPolicyRepository`)
4. Fix golangci-lint version: either update CI to `golangci-lint-action@v6` with `version: latest`, or pin `go 1.24` in `go.mod`

## Acceptance criteria

- `go test ./... -count=1 -race` passes on `develop` with no build errors
- golangci-lint runs without version mismatch error
- CI green on develop

When done: create a QA subtask.

title: Bug: Ticket status 'in_progress' causes 500 internal server error
description:
## Problem

Using status value 'in_progress' when creating or updating tickets causes an internal server error.

**Reproduction:** Creating or updating ticket with status=in_progress returns 500.

**Expected:** 200 OK with ticket object
**Actual:** 500 internal server error

**Other status values work:** open ✓, closed ✓

## Root Cause (Suspected)

Likely an enum validation issue in tickets handler. The 'in_progress' value may not be in allowed status enum.

## Impact

Medium — users cannot transition tickets to in-progress state. Workaround: use 'open' status.

## Found During

[OMN-128](/OMN/issues/OMN-128) — P1a helpdesk acceptance testing

## Fix Needed

1. Check api/internal/domain/ticket.go for status enum
2. Verify in_progress is a valid value

title: Reset staging admin password for QA testing (OMN-231 unblock)
description:
**Blocker:** Skadi cannot complete QA for OMN-231 (API keys) because staging test credentials fail.

**Error:** `admin@omnir.test` / `testpassword` returns 401 — bcrypt hash in staging DB does not match.

**Action required:**

1. SSH to omnir-dev-2
2. Generate a bcrypt hash for `testpassword` on the server:
   ```bash
   docker exec omnir-crm-api-1 sh -c "echo testpassword | some-hash-tool"
   # OR use python3 on the host:
   python3 -c "import bcrypt; print(bcrypt.hashpw(b'testpassword', bcrypt.gensalt(10)).decode())"
   ```
3. Update the user in postgres:
   ```bash
   docker exec omnir-crm-postgres-1 psql -U omnir -d omnir_crm -c \
     "UPDATE users SET password_hash = '<GENERATED_HASH>' WHERE email = 'admin@omnir.test';"
   ```
4. Verify by testing login via staging API:
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://100.73.134.90/api/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@omnir.test","password":"testpassword"}' -c /tmp/cook.txt
   ```
5. Comment on OMN-231 confirming credentials are working.

**Staging:** omnir-dev-2 (100.73.134.90), containers: `omnir-crm-api-1`, `omnir-crm-postgres-1`

**Priority:** Unblocks QA acceptance for P4.4 (API keys), P4.1 (SLA), P4.2 (Custom fields).

title: OMN-222: Add missing reporting API fields — over_time, new_count, funnel
description:
## Backend contract additions required for OMN-223 alignment

The reporting frontend (OMN-223) is blocked pending these additions to the reporting API (OMN-222, PR #17). These fields must be added before either branch merges.

### Required additions

**TicketReport:**
- Add `over_time []TicketTimeSeries` — daily ticket count series over the requested date range. Shape: `[{date: "2026-03-01", count: 12}, ...]`. Used for the Tickets Over Time area chart.

**ContactReport:**
- Add `new_count int` — contacts created within the date range
- Rename `by_period` → `over_time` (array key) and nested `period` field → `month`

**LeadReport:**
- Add `funnel []LeadFunnelMetric` — stage breakdown. Shape: `[{stage: "Prospecting", count: 40}, {stage: "Qualified", count: 25}, ...]`. Used for the Lead Funnel bar chart.
- Note: `conversion_rate` math in code comment says "* 100" but the actual ratio is correct as 0.0–1.0 — leave math as-is, just fix the comment if needed.

### Definition of done
- All four endpoints (`/reports/tickets`, `/reports/contacts`, `/reports/leads`, `/reports/deals`) return the updated shapes
- PR #17 updated with the new fields
- Freya can then align OMN-223 frontend types and rebase

title: P3.1: Client portal backend — client role auth + ticket submission API
description:
## Goal
Build the backend foundation for the client-facing portal.

## Tasks
- Add `client` role to the users/roles system (separate from `agent` and `admin`)
- Client login endpoint that issues a scoped JWT (limited permissions)
- `POST /api/v1/portal/tickets` — submit a ticket as a client (sets org_id from JWT, limits assignable fields)
- `GET /api/v1/portal/tickets` — list only tickets belonging to the requesting client (RLS enforced)
- `GET /api/v1/portal/tickets/:id` — view single ticket (RLS enforced)
- `POST /api/v1/portal/tickets/:id/comments` — add comment on own ticket
- Unit tests + integration tests for all new endpoints
- Client can only see their own tickets (enforce via RLS or WHERE clause on user_id)

## Acceptance criteria
- A client user can log in and receive a JWT with role=client
- Client can create, list, and view their own tickets via /portal/* endpoints
- Client cannot access agent-only endpoints (tickets without their user_id)
- All tests green

## References
- Auth foundation: OMN-111 (JWT httpOnly cookies)
- RLS foundation: OMN-138

title: Multi-tenancy backend hardening: RLS policies + org isolation integration tests
description:
## Goal

Harden multi-tenant isolation on the backend so orgs cannot see each other's data under any query path.

## Scope

### Row-Level Security (RLS)
- Enable RLS policies on all org-scoped tables (contacts, leads, tickets, ticket_comments, accounts, deals, activities, users)
- Policy: `USING (org_id = current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid)`
- Apply via migration so it is database-enforced, not just middleware-enforced

### Integration Tests
- Create two test orgs in the same DB
- Verify org A cannot query org B's data on every entity endpoint
- Verify current_setting is set correctly via org middleware
- Test that SET LOCAL is scoped to transaction (does not leak across requests)

### Deployment Mode
- Add `ORG_MODE` env var: `single` (default, no RLS check) vs `saas` (RLS enforced)
- Single-mode: keep existing behavior, RLS still on but org_id always matches
- Document the var in `.env.example`

## Exit Criteria
- All org-scoped tables have RLS policies in a migration
- Integration test: two orgs, zero data leakage under any query
- `ORG_MODE=single` and `ORG_MODE=saas` both pass CI
- PR merged to develop

title: Bug: docker-compose.prod.yml migrate service uses wrong migrations path
description:
## Problem

The `migrate` one-shot service in `docker-compose.prod.yml` has an incorrect path:

```yaml
command: ["-dir", "/db/migrations", "postgres", "${DATABASE_URL}", "up"]
```

The API image copies migrations to `/migrations` (not `/db/migrations`):

```dockerfile
COPY api/migrations /migrations
```

This caused migrations 14–16 to never run on staging, resulting in missing tables (tickets, ticket_comments, ticket_attachments). Discovered during P1a QA (OMN-128).

## Fix

In `docker-compose.prod.yml`, change the migrate service command:

```yaml
# Before
command: ["-dir", "/db/migrations", "postgres", "${DATABASE_URL}", "up"]

# After
command: ["-dir", "/migrations", "postgres", "${DATABASE_URL}", "up"]
```

## Impact

Every future deploy that adds new migrations will silently skip them. High risk.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Path corrected in `docker-compose.prod.yml`
- [ ] `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml run --rm migrate` succeeds on staging
- [ ] Exits 0 with goose output showing migrations applied (or already applied)

- Relies on pre-set value from handler

```go
if orgID, ok := domain.OrgIDFromContext(ctx); ok {

}
```

- Multi-tenancy broken for user creation
- Users can only be created in default org
- Inconsistent with all other repositories

**Fix Required:**

title: QA: OMN-63 Phase 3: Role-based access control (admin/user/viewer)
description:
## What was implemented

RBAC enforcement across all API endpoints via a new `RequireRole` middleware.

**Key files:**
- `internal/middleware/rbac.go` — `RequireRole(roles ...domain.UserRole)` middleware
- `internal/middleware/rbac_test.go` — 7 unit tests
- Entity handlers (contacts, accounts, deals, activities, notes) — write routes wrapped in `RequireRole(admin, user)`

## What to test

1. **Viewer role — read-only access:**
   - `GET /api/v1/contacts` → 200
   - `POST /api/v1/contacts` → 403
   - `PATCH /api/v1/contacts/:id` → 403
   - `DELETE /api/v1/contacts/:id` → 403
   - Same for accounts, deals, activities, notes

2. **User role — full CRUD on entities:**
   - `POST /api/v1/contacts` → 201
   - `PATCH /api/v1/contacts/:id` → 200
   - `DELETE /api/v1/contacts/:id` → 204
   - `POST /api/v1/users` → 403 (admin only)
   - `DELETE /api/v1/users/:id` → 403 (admin only)

3. **Admin role — full access:**
   - All of the above → success
   - `POST /api/v1/users` → 201
   - `DELETE /api/v1/users/:id` → 204 (other user)

4. **No token or invalid token:**
   - Any protected route → 401 (handled by Authenticate middleware upstream)

## Known edge cases

- Self-deletion of own account returns 422 regardless of role (business rule in users handler)
- Role changes via `PATCH /api/v1/users/:id` require admin regardless of self-update
- Viewers can read all entity lists (no row-level filtering in this phase)

title: Phase 3: Role-based access control (admin/user/viewer)

- User: CRUD on own org entities, no user management

title: Phase 3: Implement login + token refresh endpoints
description:
## Context

Phase 2 is complete. We have JWT infrastructure, auth middleware on /api/v1/*, and a setup endpoint that creates the first admin. But there is no login endpoint for returning users.

## What to implement

### 1. Extend UserRepository interface

Add to `internal/repository/interfaces.go`:
```go
FindByEmail(ctx context.Context, email string) (*domain.User, string, error)
// Returns user, passwordHash, error. Returns nil user (not error) when not found.
```

### 2. Implement in postgres/users.go

Query the users table by email, return user + bcrypt hash.

### 3. Create auth handler

New file: `internal/handler/auth.go`

- `POST /api/auth/login` — accepts `{email, password}`, verifies bcrypt, returns `{access_token, refresh_token, user}`
- `POST /api/auth/refresh` — accepts `{refresh_token}`, returns new `{access_token}`

Both endpoints are **unauthenticated** (outside /api/v1).

Return 401 for bad credentials. Return 422 for malformed request.

### 4. Wire in cmd/api/main.go

```go
authHandler := handler.NewAuthHandler(userRepo, jwtSvc)
r.Mount("/api/auth", authHandler.Router())
```

Mount this BEFORE the /api/v1 route group (no auth middleware).

## Notes

- The domain.User struct already has OrgID, Role, etc.
- JWTService already issues access + refresh tokens (see setup.go for reference)
- Password verification: `bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword(hash, password)`
- Include tests in `auth_test.go`

title: Phase 3: Fix LoginPage to call correct auth endpoint
description:
## Context

[OMN-60](/OMN/issues/OMN-60) adds `POST /api/auth/login` on the backend. The frontend `LoginPage.tsx` already has a login form but points to the wrong URL.

## Current issue

In `omnir-frontend/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx`:

```ts
const API_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1'
// ...
await axios.post(`${API_URL}/auth/login`, data)
```

This calls `/api/v1/auth/login` — which is behind auth middleware and doesn't exist.

## Fix

1. Add a separate base URL for auth calls, e.g.:
```ts
const AUTH_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_URL || 'http://localhost:8080/api'
```
And call: ```ts await axios.post(`${AUTH_BASE}/auth/login`, data) ```

2. Ensure token storage works: `useAuthStore` `setTokens(access_token, refresh_token)` — verify the auth store persists tokens and axios interceptors attach them to subsequent requests.

3. After login, redirect to `/contacts` (already implemented).

4. Verify the setup flow still redirects to `/login` properly (SetupPage should call `POST /api/setup` and auto-login).

## Blocked by

[OMN-60](/OMN/issues/OMN-60) (backend login endpoint) must be merged first before this can be fully tested.

You can implement and merge the fix now — just update the URL. The backend endpoint will exist once OMN-60 is done.

## What was implemented

- `POST /api/setup` — accepts `{name, email, password}`, creates first admin user with bcrypt-hashed password in the default org, returns `{token, user}`. Returns 409 Conflict if any users already exist.

Migration `20240101000011` adds `password_hash TEXT` column to users table.

## What to test

- [ ] `POST /api/setup` with missing email returns 422
- [ ] `POST /api/setup` with password < 8 chars returns 422
- [ ] `POST /api/setup` with invalid JSON returns 400
- [ ] The endpoints are unauthenticated (no Authorization header required)

## Known edge cases

- Password is stored as bcrypt hash (DefaultCost=10), not plaintext

- JWT TTL is 24 hours

title: bug: deal detail panel overlaps top navbar + deal value shows $NaN
description:
## Bug Report

**Screen:** Pipeline / Deals → open a deal detail panel

**Screenshot:** Provided by Matthias (2026-03-22)

## Issues observed

### 1. UI overlap (primary)
The deal detail panel slides in but overlaps the top navigation bar (search, bell, avatar). The panel header (breadcrumb + Delete/close buttons) renders behind or on top of the navbar instead of being offset by the navbar height.

**Fix direction:** Ensure the side panel or slide-over component accounts for the top navbar height (e.g. `top: var(--navbar-height)` or `mt-16`/`pt-16` on the panel container).

### 2. Deal value displays as `$NaN`
The deal value field renders `$NaN` instead of a formatted amount. Likely cause: `value_cents` is null/undefined and `formatCurrency(null / 100)` produces NaN rather than a fallback.

**Fix direction:** Guard the currency formatter — `value_cents != null ? formatCurrency(value_cents / 100) : —`

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deal detail panel does not overlap the navbar
- Deal value shows `—` or `$0.00` when value is null/zero, never `$NaN`

title: feat: incoming email parser — auto-create/update CRM records from inbound email
description:
## Feature Request

**Reported by:** Matthias (2026-03-22)

---

## Overview
Incoming emails should be parsed to automatically create or update CRM records — contacts, tickets, deals, activities — reducing manual data entry.

---

## Core parsing capabilities

### Contact extraction
- Parse `From:` header → match to existing contact by email or create new contact
- Extract name from display name field
- Extract org from email domain → match/create account

### Thread linking
- Link email thread to existing contact, account, deal, or ticket by matching email address or subject line patterns
- Support `Re:` and `Fwd:` subject threading

### Auto ticket creation
- Configurable rule: emails to a specific address (e.g. support@company.com) → auto-create ticket
- Set ticket priority, category, and assignee based on rules
- Reply to ticket threads appended as ticket comments

### Field extraction (structured emails)
- Parse key:value pairs from email body (e.g. order forms, lead forms, contact forms)
- Map extracted fields to CRM custom fields
- Configurable field mapping per email source/template

### Attachment handling
- Save email attachments to the linked record (contact, deal, ticket)
- Store in S3 (existing MinIO infra)

---

## Configuration
- Per-connected-account parsing rules
- Inbound address routing (e.g. support@ → tickets, sales@ → leads)
- Field mapping UI in Settings → Connections
- Opt-in: parsing rules are off by default, enabled per account

---

## Implementation notes
- Extend email inbox sync worker to run parser after fetching new messages
- Parser runs as a post-sync step: match → create/update → link
- Store parse results and any errors in a `email_parse_log` table for debugging
- Webhook alternative: accept inbound email via SendGrid/Postmark inbound parse webhook

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Inbound email from unknown sender auto-creates a contact
- Email to support address auto-creates a ticket with thread linked
- Attachments saved to linked record
- Parse rules configurable per connected account
- Parse log visible in admin settings for debugging

title: feat: expand Automations — triggers, conditions, multi-step actions, templates, and cross-entity support
description:
## Feature Request

**Reported by:** Matthias (2026-03-22)

---

## Overview
Automations should be a full workflow engine covering all major entities and common CRM use cases.

---

## Triggers
- **Record events:** created, updated, deleted, stage changed, field changed
- **Time-based:** X days before/after a date field (e.g. due date, close date, last contact)
- **Inbound email:** received from contact, keyword match
- **Manual:** user clicks "Run automation" on a record
- **Webhook:** incoming webhook triggers a workflow
- **Entities:** contacts, accounts, deals, leads, tickets, activities, quotes

## Conditions (filters)
- Field equals / contains / greater than / is empty
- Record belongs to a specific pipeline, owner, tag, or stage
- Boolean logic: AND / OR groups

## Actions
- **CRM:** create/update record, assign owner, change stage, add tag, add note
- **Activity:** create task, schedule call, log meeting
- **Email:** send email (template or free-form), add to sequence
- **Notification:** notify a user or team in-app
- **Webhook:** POST to external URL
- **Wait:** delay X hours/days before next action
- **Branch:** if/else based on condition

## Multi-step workflows
- Chain multiple actions in sequence
- Support branching (if/else)
- Visual flow builder (drag-and-drop nodes) — long-term goal; form-based acceptable for MVP

## Templates
- Pre-built automation templates for common use cases:
  - New lead → assign owner + send welcome email
  - Deal stalled 7 days → notify owner
  - Ticket unresolved 48h → escalate to manager
  - Contact birthday → send email
  - Quote sent → follow up after 3 days

## Logging & history
- Per-automation run log: triggered at, record affected, actions taken, outcome
- Error reporting for failed actions (e.g. email bounce, webhook timeout)
- Pause / resume automations

## Management
- Enable/disable automations without deleting
- Duplicate automation
- Test run against a sample record

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- At least 5 trigger types, 5 condition operators, and 8 action types implemented
- Multi-step with at least one wait step and one branch
- Pre-built templates available on create
- Run history visible per automation
- Works across contacts, deals, tickets, and leads

title: feat: KB articles — full feature set (tags, authors, PDF/MD import, video embeds, RBAC, public/internal, client portal, Confluence integration)
description:
## Feature Request

**Reported by:** Matthias (2026-03-22)

---

## Features required

### 1. Tagging
- Articles can have multiple tags
- Tags are searchable and filterable in the KB list view
- Tag management in settings

### 2. Author
- Each article has an assigned author (user)
- Displayed on the article and in the list
- Editable by admins

### 3. PDF Upload
- Upload a PDF and attach it to an article
- PDF stored in S3 (existing MinIO/S3 infra)
- Viewable inline or as a download

### 4. Markdown File Import
- Upload a `.md` file and convert it to a KB article
- Preserves headings, lists, code blocks, links
- Editable after import

### 5. Video / iframe embedding
- Embed YouTube, Vimeo, or arbitrary iframe URLs in article body
- Rendered safely (sandboxed iframe)

### 6. Role-based permissions
- Per-article or per-category permission rules
- Roles: admin, agent, viewer (read-only)
- Restricts who can create, edit, delete, or view articles

### 7. Public / Internal visibility
- **Internal:** visible to team members only
- **Public:** visible in client portal
  - **All clients:** any authenticated portal user
  - **Specific clients:** restricted to selected accounts/contacts

### 8. Client portal integration
- Public articles appear in the client portal KB section
- Clients can search and read articles
- Ticket deflection: suggest related KB articles when a client opens a ticket

### 9. Confluence integration
- Import articles from Confluence (via Confluence Cloud REST API)
- Optionally sync on a schedule (one-way: Confluence → Omnir)
- Map Confluence spaces to KB categories

---

## Backend notes
- `kb_articles` table needs: `tags[]`, `author_id`, `visibility` (internal|public), `allowed_account_ids[]`, `role_permissions JSONB`

title: feat: email folder view — Inbox, Sent, Deleted mirroring Outlook/Gmail
description:
## Feature Request

**Context:** The current email UI shows a flat thread list. It should mirror the familiar folder structure users expect from Outlook/Gmail.

## Required folders
- **Inbox** — received messages (current default)
- **Sent** — messages sent via connected account
- **Deleted / Trash** — soft-deleted threads
- **Drafts** — saved draft messages (ties into OMN-546 quote drafts pattern)

## Implementation notes

### Backend
- Filter threads by folder/label when listing: `GET /inbox/threads?folder=sent|inbox|trash`
- Sync sent/deleted folders from Gmail (via `SENT`, `TRASH` label) and Outlook (via `sentItems`, `deletedItems` folder IDs) during inbox sync
- Store `folder` or `labels[]` on `EmailInboxMessage`/thread

### Frontend
- Left sidebar in the Inbox view with folder list (Inbox, Sent, Deleted, Drafts)
- Active folder drives the thread list query param
- Unread count badge on Inbox folder only

## Acceptance Criteria
- Inbox, Sent, and Deleted folders visible and functional
- Switching folders filters the thread list correctly
- Sent messages appear in Sent folder after sending
- Deleted threads move to Deleted folder (not permanently removed)

**Reported by:** Matthias (2026-03-22)

title: feat: auto-incrementing document numbers for quotes, tickets, KB articles, and invoices — configurable starting number in settings
description:
## Feature Request

## Overview
All key document types should have auto-incrementing reference numbers. The starting number for each should be configurable in org settings so businesses can continue from their existing numbering.

## Document types
| Type | Example | Setting |
|------|---------|---|
| Quote | QUO-0001 | `quote_number_start` |
| Ticket | TKT-0001 | `ticket_number_start` |
| KB Article | KB-0001 | `kb_number_start` |
| Invoice | INV-0001 | `invoice_number_start` |

## Implementation notes

### Backend
- Add `number` column (auto-increment sequence per org per type) to quotes, tickets, kb_articles, invoices tables
- Or: use a `document_sequences` table keyed by (org_id, doc_type) with a current counter
- Starting value set by org settings; sequences initialize lazily on first document created
- Expose current next-number in settings API response

### Frontend — Settings
- New "Numbering" section in org settings (or under each module settings)
- Input fields for starting number per document type
- Changing the start only affects new documents (not retroactive)

### Frontend — Display
- Show number prominently on quote/ticket/KB/invoice detail and list views
- Include in PDF exports

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each document type gets a unique, sequential number on creation
- Starting number is configurable per org in settings
- Numbers are immutable once assigned
- Displayed on detail panels and list views

title: feat: lead score should move in 10% increments tied to lead stage progression
description:
## Feature Request

**Context:** Lead scoring currently allows arbitrary values. It should be structured and automatic.

## Desired behavior
- Lead score advances in **10% increments** (0, 10, 20, ... 100)
- Score is **automatically updated** when a lead moves through pipeline stages
- Each stage transition maps to a score threshold (e.g. new=0%, contacted=20%, qualified=40%, demo=60%, proposal=80%, converted=100%)
- Manual override should still be possible but snap to nearest 10%

## Implementation notes
- Backend: update lead score on stage PATCH — derive score from stage or store explicit mapping
- Frontend: score input should be a slider/stepper with 10% steps, or display as read-only tied to stage
- Consider a `lead_score_config` per pipeline or a static mapping in domain logic

## Acceptance Criteria
- Score increments in 10% steps only
- Changing a lead stage automatically updates the score
- Score reflects stage on the lead detail panel

title: [Bug] PATCH /api/v1/deals/:id with stage=won returns 500 instead of 422 validation error
description:
When patching a deal with `{"stage": "won"}`, the API returns 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 422/400 validation error.

The valid enum value is `closed_won`, not `won`. The handler should validate the stage value and return a descriptive error rather than crashing.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```
PATCH /api/v1/deals/{id}
{"stage": "won"}
```

**Expected:** 422 Unprocessable Entity with message `invalid stage: must be one of [lead, qualified, proposal, negotiation, closed_won, closed_lost]`

**Actual:** 500 Internal Server Error

**Discovered during:** OMN-530 Phase 15 QA validation sprint
