title: Implement Pipeline (Kanban + List) and Reports Dashboard pages
description:
Implement the Pipeline and Reports Dashboard pages per the UX spec in OMN-468.

**Spec:** See OMN-468 comments for the full spec authored by Saga.

## Pipeline Page

### Requirements
- Kanban board view (default): columns per stage, deal cards with value/contact/age, drag-and-drop stage changes
- List view toggle: TanStack Table, sortable columns, pagination (25/page)
- Filter bar: Stage, Owner, Priority, Date Range dropdowns → active filter chips → Clear all
- New Deal slide-over panel (right side)
- URL search param persistence: `?view=board|list`
- Mobile: horizontal scroll columns, tap-to-move bottom sheet (no DnD on touch)

### Key technical choices (pre-approved by Völundr)
- DnD: `@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/sortable` — install if not present. Do NOT use react-beautiful-dnd.
- Optimistic updates: `useMutation` with `onMutate`/`onError` rollback via TanStack Query
- View persistence: TanStack Router `useSearch` for `?view=board|list`
- Large columns (>15 cards): virtual scroll with `@tanstack/react-virtual`, not hard truncation
- Column min-width: 200px floor (240px preferred), flex-shrink on narrow viewports

## Reports Dashboard

### Requirements
- KPI summary row: Total Revenue, New Deals, Closed Won, Resolution Rate (4-card grid)
- Widget 1: Pipeline Funnel — `Recharts FunnelChart`, gradient `#1B3A4B` → `#7C8DB0`
- Widget 2: Revenue Over Time — `Recharts ComposedChart` (bars + trend line), dynamic X-axis intervals
- Widget 3: Ticket Resolution Rates — `Recharts LineChart`, 3 series (Resolved/Pending/Escalated), color+dash differentiation
- Date range picker: Last 7/30/90d, This Quarter/Year, Custom Range (refetches all charts)
- Export: CSV (flat file) + PDF (html2canvas, flag as MVP quality)

### Accessibility (required, not optional)
- SVG `<title>` + `<desc>` on all charts
- "View as table" toggle for each chart (WCAG 1.1.1)
- ARIA roles on filter dropdowns, view switcher, date picker, export menu
- Keyboard drag alternative on Pipeline (Space to pick up, Arrow keys to move, Space to drop)
- Resolution Rate chart: color + dash pattern for color-blind users

## Design Tokens (PraestOS)
- Primary: `#1B3A4B`, Text: `#1A1D23`, Secondary: `#6B7280`, Border: `#E5E7EB`, Active bg: `#E8EDF2`
- Font: Inter, Radius: 8px, Focus ring: `2px solid #1B3A4B`

title: Implement: Dashboard overview page (PraestOS design language)
description:
Implement the dashboard overview page per the approved UX spec in OMN-465.

## Reference
See OMN-465 comments for the full spec. Summary below.

## Components to build

### KPI Row (4 cards)
- Total Revenue, Pipeline Value, Active Deals, Open Tickets
- White card, 1px #E5E7EB border, border-radius 8px, padding 20px 24px
- Value: 36px bold #1A1D23; label: 11px uppercase #7C8DB0
- Trend pill: ↑/↓ percent in green/red + "vs last month" in #6B7280 12px
- No trend pill if prior-period data unavailable

### Revenue Bar Chart (col-span 3 of 4)
- Use Recharts `BarChart`; bars fill `#7C8DB0`, hover `#1B3A4B`
- Month selector dropdown (shadcn Select), default "Last 6 months"
- Chart height 240px desktop, 180px mobile
- Min bar height 2px (zero-value months)
- Animate bars in on first render: CSS `scaleY` from 0, 200ms ease-out, 30ms stagger

### Quick Actions Card (2×2 grid)
- Buttons: Add Lead (UserPlus), Schedule (CalendarPlus), Email (Mail), Invoice (FileText)
- Invoice: not yet routed — show `toast("Coming soon")` + visual "soon" badge
- Hover: #F7F8FA bg, border #1B3A4B

### Tasks Checklist Card
- "My Tasks" title + "+ Add task" link (right-aligned)
- Checkbox + label + due date; overdue in #EF4444
- Optimistic check-off with strikethrough + fade to #6B7280
- Max 8 visible; "View all tasks →" link
- Empty state: illustration + "No tasks yet. Add one above."

### Activity Feed Card
- "Recent Activity" title
- Icon circle (40px, #E8EDF2 bg, #1B3A4B icon) + body text + timestamp
- Icons per entity type: ticket=Ticket, contact=User, deal=TrendingUp, email=Mail, note=StickyNote
- Rows are `<a>` links to entity pages; deleted entities: greyed row, italics "Deleted record", not clickable
- Max 10 items; "Load more" text link

## Data / Queries
- TanStack Query: `staleTime: 60_000`, `refetchInterval: 60_000`
- No skeleton re-render on background refetch — show `Updating...` badge (top-right of main content, 11px #7C8DB0) while refetch in flight

## States
- Loading: skeleton cards with animate-pulse, fixed dimensions matching live cards
- Empty: `—` values, no trend pill, "No data yet" in chart, empty state copy per card
- Error: inline `⚠ Failed to load. Retry ↺` per card; retry calls `refetch()` on that query key

## Mobile (< 640px)
- KPI: 2-column grid; full-width below 400px
- Chart: full width, 180px height
- All cards stack vertically

## Accessibility
- KPI cards: `<article>` with descriptive `aria-label`
- Chart: `role="img"` + visually-hidden `<table>` for screen readers
- Quick Actions: `<button>` with `aria-label`
- Tasks: shadcn Checkbox with `htmlFor`
- Activity feed: `<ul role="list">` with `<li>` + `<a>` rows
- Focus ring: 2px solid #1B3A4B on all interactive elements
- Skeleton: `aria-busy="true"` on parent, `aria-hidden="true"` on shimmer elements

## Route
`/dashboard` — default route after auth

When done, mark this issue done and create a QA subtask for Skadi.

App Shell Component Create `web/src/components/shell/AppShell.tsx`: - Fixed sidebar (210px) + top bar (56px) layout - Content area: `bg: #F7F8FA`, 24px padding, takes remaining space - Wrap all authenticated routes in AppShell via TanStack Router layout route - Unauthenticated → redirect to `/login` before mount ### 3. title: Phase 13 / Enrichment: Contact enrichment backend (domain lookup, enrichment cache, Clearbit/Hunter fallback)
description:
## Context

Phase 13 Area 3 (backend). Auto-enrichment from email domain reduces contact data entry friction — the biggest time sink for sales reps.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE enrichment_cache (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  domain TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  data JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  source TEXT NOT NULL,  -- clearbit | hunter | dns | manual
  fetched_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL  -- fetched_at + 30 days
);
CREATE INDEX ON enrichment_cache(domain);
CREATE INDEX ON enrichment_cache(expires_at);

ALTER TABLE contacts ADD COLUMN enriched_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE contacts ADD COLUMN enrichment_source TEXT;
```

## Scope

1. **Enrichment worker** — on contact create/update with email: extract domain, check cache (respect TTL), if miss → query enrichment APIs in priority order
2. **Enrichment API priority chain:**
   - If `CLEARBIT_API_KEY` configured: Clearbit Enrichment API (company + person data)
   - Else if `HUNTER_API_KEY` configured: Hunter.io Suggest API
   - Else: basic DNS/MX lookup (identifies domain, ISP, country) — always available
3. **Data mapping:** fill contact's `company`, account link suggestion, `custom_fields.linkedin_url`, `custom_fields.company_industry`, `custom_fields.company_size` from enrichment data
4. **Async processing** — contact saves immediately; enrichment runs in background goroutine; updates contact when complete
5. **API endpoints:**
   - `POST /api/v1/contacts/:id/enrich` — manual trigger
   - `GET /api/v1/contacts/:id/enrichment` — status + data for current contact
   - `GET /api/v1/enrichment/cache/:domain` — admin: view cached domain data
   - `DELETE /api/v1/enrichment/cache/:domain` — admin: bust cache for domain
6. **Configuration:** `CLEARBIT_API_KEY`, `HUNTER_API_KEY` optional env vars; feature enabled regardless (DNS fallback always works)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating a contact with an email address triggers background enrichment
- Enriched fields auto-populate on contact record (non-destructively: only fill empty fields)
- Cache TTL 30 days — same domain not re-fetched within TTL
- Manual `POST /enrich` respects cooldown (no re-enrich if enriched_at < 24h ago)
- Works without any external API keys (DNS fallback)
- QA subtask created when done

title: Phase 12: Knowledge Base — backend API (articles, categories, full-text search)
description:
## Objective

Build the backend for the Knowledge Base / self-service help center. Enables article management and public ticket deflection.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE kb_categories (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    org_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES orgs(id),
    name       TEXT NOT NULL,
    slug       TEXT NOT NULL,
    position   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (org_id, slug)
);

CREATE TABLE kb_articles (
    id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    org_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES orgs(id),
    category_id   UUID REFERENCES kb_categories(id),
    title         TEXT NOT NULL,
    slug          TEXT NOT NULL,
    body          TEXT NOT NULL,  -- markdown
    status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT draft,  -- draft | published
    view_count    INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    search_vector TSVECTOR GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        to_tsvector(english, title ||   || body)
    ) STORED,
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    deleted_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    UNIQUE (org_id, slug)
);

CREATE INDEX ON kb_articles USING GIN (search_vector);
```

## API Endpoints

**Admin (authenticated):**
- `GET /api/v1/kb/categories` — list categories
- `POST /api/v1/kb/categories` — create category
- `PATCH /api/v1/kb/categories/{id}` — update
- `DELETE /api/v1/kb/categories/{id}` — soft delete
- `GET /api/v1/kb/articles` — list (filter by status, category)
- `POST /api/v1/kb/articles` — create
- `GET /api/v1/kb/articles/{id}` — detail
- `PATCH /api/v1/kb/articles/{id}` — update (publish/unpublish, edit body)
- `DELETE /api/v1/kb/articles/{id}` — soft delete

**Public (no auth required):**
- `GET /api/public/kb/{orgSlug}/articles?q=...` — full-text search (tsvector)
- `GET /api/public/kb/{orgSlug}/articles/{slug}` — article detail (increments view_count)
- `GET /api/public/kb/{orgSlug}/categories` — category list with article counts

**Ticket deflection:**
- `GET /api/v1/kb/articles/suggest?q=...` — returns top 3 articles by relevance for ticket subject

## Owner
Tyr (backend). Freya consumes in OMN-440.

title: UX: Reports page — empty state shows broken cards + flash of demo data
description:
Two issues on the Reports page when the database is empty:

1. **Flash of demo data**: Sample/placeholder data appears briefly then disappears, which looks like a loading bug rather than intentional behavior.

2. **Empty state is broken**: After the flash, all metric cards show just a colored line with no values. The error banner "Some report data could not be loaded" is vague and unhelpful. The page looks broken rather than empty.

**Expected behavior for empty database:**
- Show a clear empty state: "No data yet — reports will populate as you add contacts, deals, and tickets"
- OR show example/sample data with a visible watermark/banner: "Sample data — add real records to see your metrics"
- No flash of content that disappears
- Metric cards should show "0" or "—" with proper formatting, not broken chart fragments

**Design guidance:**
- Empty state illustration or icon
- Call-to-action: "Create your first contact" / "Open your first ticket"
- If showing sample data, use a distinct visual treatment (grey overlay, "SAMPLE" badge, dashed borders)
- Error banner should be specific about what failed, or not shown at all if the DB is simply empty

title: Phase 9 Area 4: SLA Engine
description:
## Context

Enterprise CRM users need service-level agreements on deals and tickets. Without SLAs, there is no way to enforce response or resolution time commitments.

## Task

Implement an SLA engine that can define, track, and alert on SLA breaches for deals and activities.

### Backend (Tyr)

1. **Schema**
   - `sla_policies` table: `id`, `org_id`, `name`, `entity_type` (deal/contact/activity), `conditions` JSONB (e.g. priority=high), `response_time_minutes`, `resolution_time_minutes`, `created_at`
   - `sla_instances` table: `id`, `org_id`, `policy_id`, `entity_id`, `entity_type`, `started_at`, `response_due_at`, `resolution_due_at`, `responded_at`, `resolved_at`, `breached` bool, `breach_type` (response/resolution/none), `created_at`
   - Migrations: `021_sla_policies.sql`, `022_sla_instances.sql`

2. **SLA lifecycle**
   - On deal/activity create: evaluate all matching policies, create sla_instance rows
   - On deal update (stage change, activity logged): update responded_at/resolved_at if criteria met
   - Background worker (goroutine + ticker, every 5min): scan open instances, mark breached where due_at < now

3. **API endpoints**
   - `GET/POST /api/sla-policies` — list/create
   - `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/sla-policies/:id` — get/update/delete
   - `GET /api/sla-instances?entityId=...&breached=true` — list
   - `GET /api/sla-dashboard` — summary: on-track count, at-risk count, breached count

4. **Notifications**
   - Emit notification (use existing notifications system from Phase 7) when:
     - SLA is 80% elapsed (warning)
     - SLA is breached
   - Assign to the deal owner

### Frontend (Freya)

1. **Admin: SLA Policy manager** (`/settings/sla`)
   - List, create, edit, delete policies
   - Form: name, entity type, conditions builder (simple: priority dropdown), response/resolution time

2. **Deal detail: SLA indicator**
   - Badge showing: On Track / At Risk / Breached
   - Hover: shows time remaining or elapsed since breach

3. **SLA Dashboard widget** (add to existing dashboard)
   - Count cards: On Track / At Risk / Breached
   - Link to filtered deals list

### Exit criteria
- Admins can define SLA policies with time thresholds
- Deals automatically get SLA instances on creation
- Breach detection runs on schedule, triggers notifications
- Dashboard shows SLA health at a glance
- QA subtask created when done

title: P8.3: API rate limiting + audit log — backend
description:
## Goal
Security hardening before user growth: per-org rate limits on the API, and an admin-visible audit trail of CRM mutations.

## Part 1: Rate Limiting
Use in-memory sliding window (or Redis if available) in Chi middleware.

```go
// middleware/ratelimit.go
// Per org_id: 1000 req/min (configurable via env RATE_LIMIT_RPM)
// 429 response: { "error": "rate limit exceeded", "retry_after": 60 }
```

- Extract org_id from JWT claims in middleware
- Apply after auth middleware, before route handlers
- Skip rate limiting for /health, /api/auth/*
- Log rate limit hits to stdout

## Part 2: Audit Log
```sql
CREATE TABLE audit_logs (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  actor_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  action TEXT NOT NULL,  -- e.g. 'contact.create', 'deal.update', 'lead.convert'
  entity_type TEXT,
  entity_id UUID,
  changes JSONB,         -- before/after snapshot for updates
  ip_address TEXT,
  user_agent TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_logs_org ON audit_logs (org_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_logs_entity ON audit_logs (org_id, entity_type, entity_id);
```

- Write audit log entries from handlers on: create, update, delete, convert
- New endpoint: `GET /api/v1/audit-logs?entity_type=&entity_id=&page=&per_page=` (admin only)
- Trim logs older than 90 days via goose migration or cron

## Notes
- Rate limiter should be a clean Chi middleware (not tied to specific routes)
- Audit log writes should be async (goroutine + recover) so they don't block requests

`GET /api/reports/pipeline-funnel?pipelineId=<id>&from=<date>&to=<date>`
Returns count + total_value_cents per stage:
```json
{"stages": [{"name": "Lead", "count": 42, "value_cents": 1200000}, ...]}
```

### Conversion Rates
`GET /api/reports/conversion-rates?from=<date>&to=<date>`
For each consecutive stage pair: deals that moved forward vs total entered that stage.
```json
{"rates": [{"from": "Lead", "to": "Qualified", "rate": 0.62}, ...]}
```

### Revenue Projections
`GET /api/reports/revenue-projection?months=3`
Groups open deals by expected_close_date bucket (current month, +1, +2...) with sum of value_cents weighted by stage probability.
```json
{"months": [{"month": "2026-04", "projected_cents": 840000, "deal_count": 7}, ...]}
```

### Activity Summary
`GET /api/reports/activity-summary?from=<date>&to=<date>`
Count by kind (call/email/meeting/task) and by owner.

## Notes
- All endpoints scoped to company_id from JWT
- Use read replicas if available; these are expensive queries
- Add DB indexes for date range scans on deals.expected_close_date and activities.created_at if missing
- Cache results for 5 minutes (in-memory, keyed by company+params)

title: Backend: DB performance review — indexes, query plans, N+1 audit
description:
## Context

With Phase 1–5 complete and multi-tenancy (RLS + org_id) fully wired, this is a good time to audit DB performance before the product sees real load.

## Tasks

### 1. Index audit
- Run `\d` on all key tables (contacts, accounts, deals, tickets, activities, users, orgs)
- Check for missing indexes on: `org_id` columns, foreign keys, common filter columns (email, status, created_at)
- Add any missing indexes via migration

### 2. N+1 query check
- Review handlers that return lists (contacts list, deals list, ticket list)
- Ensure joins or preloads are used, not per-row queries
- Check activity/timeline queries on contact/deal detail pages

### 3. Slow query log
- Enable `log_min_duration_statement = 100` temporarily in staging
- Run the QA test suite and capture slow queries
- Fix or add TODO comments on anything > 100ms

### 4. Pagination review
- Ensure all list endpoints use `LIMIT/OFFSET` or cursor pagination
- No endpoints should return unbounded result sets

## Acceptance criteria
- All tables have indexes on `org_id` (RLS performance)
- No obvious N+1 in core list views
- Pagination enforced on all list endpoints
- Document findings in `docs/db-performance-notes.md`

title: P5.1: Global search backend — full-text search across tickets, contacts, accounts, deals
description:
Implement a global search API endpoint that searches across all core CRM entities.

## Requirements

### Endpoint
`GET /api/v1/search?q=<query>&limit=20`

### Response format
```json
{
  "results": [
    { "type": "ticket", "id": "...", "title": "...", "excerpt": "...", "url": "/tickets/{id}" },
    { "type": "contact", "id": "...", "title": "John Doe", "excerpt": "john@acme.com", "url": "/contacts/{id}" },
    { "type": "account", ... },
    { "type": "deal", ... }
  ],
  "total": 42
}
```

### Search scope
- Tickets: title, description, comments
- Contacts: name, email, phone, company
- Accounts: name, domain, description
- Deals: title, description

### Implementation
- Use PostgreSQL `to_tsvector` + `plainto_tsquery` for full-text search
- Add GIN indexes on all searchable columns
- Org-scoped results (RLS / org_id filter)
- Migration: add tsvector columns + GIN indexes

## Acceptance Criteria
- `GET /api/v1/search?q=acme` returns tickets, contacts, accounts, deals matching "acme"
- Results are org-scoped (no cross-org leakage)
- Response time < 200ms for typical queries

title: P4.4: API key management — schema + CRUD + auth middleware
description:
Implement API key management so external clients can authenticate without a JWT session.

## Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE api_keys (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  org_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id),
  created_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  key_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  key_prefix TEXT NOT NULL,
  scopes TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}',
  last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

## Endpoints
- `POST /api/v1/api-keys` — create (returns full key once only)
- `GET /api/v1/api-keys` — list (prefix, name, last_used)
- `DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/:id` — revoke

## Auth middleware
- Accept `Authorization: Bearer ak_<key>` alongside JWT
- Resolve org_id + user context from api_key row
- Update last_used_at on each request

## Constraints
- Admin-only create/delete
- Keys are SHA-256 hashed at rest; plaintext only shown on creation
- Expired/revoked keys return 401

## Ref
- [OMN-122](/OMN/issues/OMN-122) — Phase 4 parent

title: Fix button touch target accessibility (OMN-105 finding)
description:
## Issue

Default button height is 36px, below WCAG 2.1 AA minimum touch target size of 44px.

**Current implementation:**
```typescript
size: {
  default: 'h-9 px-4 py-2',  // 36px
  sm: 'h-8 px-3 text-xs',      // 32px
  lg: 'h-11 rounded-md px-8',  // 44px ✓
  icon: 'h-9 w-9',             // 36px
}
```

## Fix

Update `components/ui/Button.tsx:19` to meet 44px minimum:

**Option 1:** Change default to `h-11`
```typescript
default: 'h-11 px-4 py-2',  // 44px
```

**Option 2:** Add min-height
```typescript
default: 'h-9 px-4 py-2 min-h-[44px]',
```

**Impact:** All buttons across app (Add Contact, pagination, filters, modals, etc.)

## Exit Criteria
- Default button meets 44px touch target
- Visual appearance remains acceptable
- No layout regressions
- Frontend build passes

**Recommended assignee:** @Freya (frontend engineer)

description:

- **Repo**: `NotificationRepository` — `Create`, `MarkRead`, `ListByUser`, `GenerateReminders`
- **Worker**: `ReminderWorker` — 1-minute ticker, bulk INSERT with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
- **Endpoints**:
  - `GET /api/notifications` — list for authenticated user; supports `?unread=true`, `?page`, `?limit`
  - `PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read` — mark as read (returns 204)

### What to test
- [ ] Migration applies cleanly
- [ ] `GET /api/notifications` returns 200 with paginated response, scoped to current user
- [ ] `?unread=true` filters out read notifications
- [ ] `PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read` returns 204; subsequent GET shows `read_at` set
- [ ] `PATCH` returns 404 for unknown/other-user notifications
- [ ] Worker creates `upcoming_1d` notification ~1 day before activity due date
- [ ] Worker creates `overdue` notification for past-due incomplete activities

title: Bug: Search shortcut shows ⌘K on all platforms — should be platform-dependent
description:
The global search bar shows "Search... (⌘K)" which is macOS-specific.

On Windows/Linux it should show "Search... (Ctrl+K)".

Fix: Detect platform via navigator.platform or navigator.userAgentData and render the appropriate modifier key.

```tsx
const isMac = typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && /Mac|iPod|iPhone|iPad/.test(navigator.platform)
const shortcutLabel = isMac ? '⌘K' : 'Ctrl+K'
```

Apply to the search input placeholder in the header/navbar component.

title: Phase 8 / Saved Searches + Views: backend API
description:
## Context

Deferred from Phase 7. Users need to save filter combinations, pin named views, and share them across the team. This issue covers the backend API.

## Schema (new migration)

```sql
CREATE TABLE saved_views (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  created_by    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  entity_type   TEXT NOT NULL,  -- contacts | accounts | deals | leads
  name          TEXT NOT NULL,
  filters       JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT {},
  sort_by       TEXT,
  sort_dir      TEXT CHECK (sort_dir IN (asc, desc)),
  is_shared     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  is_pinned     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  pinned_order  INTEGER,
  deleted_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX ON saved_views(org_id, entity_type) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
```

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/views?entityType={type}` — list views visible to current user (own + shared), ordered by pinned_order then name
- `POST /api/views` — create view `{entityType, name, filters, sortBy, sortDir, isShared, isPinned}`
- `PATCH /api/views/{id}` — update any field
- `DELETE /api/views/{id}` — soft delete (own views only, or admin)
- `POST /api/views/{id}/pin` — pin/unpin toggle, reorder pinned_order

## Filter schema

Filters JSONB is an array of filter objects: `[{field: "stage", op: "eq", value: "lead"}, ...]`. This is frontend-interpreted; backend stores opaquely.

## Access control

- Users can read their own views + all shared views in their org
- Only creator (or admin) can edit/delete
- `is_shared=true` views are visible to all org members

## Tests

CRUD tests, access control (can't edit other user's private view), pin ordering.

## Exit criteria

- All 5 endpoints implemented and tested
- Migration applied cleanly
- QA subtask created when done

title: Phase 9 Area 3: Client Portal (External Access)
description:
## Context

Sales teams need to share deal progress, documents, and next steps with their clients without giving clients full CRM access. A client portal provides a read-only, branded, shareable view of selected deal information.

## Task

Build a client-facing portal: external users (no CRM account) can view a shared deal page via a secure link.

### Backend (Tyr)

1. **Schema** — new `portal_links` table:
   - `id`, `org_id`, `deal_id`, `created_by_user_id`, `token` (random 32 bytes, URL-safe), `label`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`, `view_count`, `last_viewed_at`, `created_at`
   - Migration: `020_portal_links.sql`

2. **API endpoints**
   - `POST /api/deals/:dealId/portal-links` — create link (org members only)
   - `GET /api/deals/:dealId/portal-links` — list links for deal
   - `DELETE /api/portal-links/:id` — revoke
   - `GET /api/portal/:token` — public endpoint, no auth required; returns deal snapshot
   - Increment `view_count` + `last_viewed_at` on portal access

3. **Access controls**
   - Portal endpoint bypasses JWT middleware (token IS the credential)
   - Never expose internal IDs, org data, or other deals
   - Revoked/expired links return 404 (not 401 — do not leak existence)

### Frontend (Freya)

**Internal UI:**
- Deal detail page: Share button -> creates portal link, shows copy URL modal
- Link management: list active links, revoke, see view count

**Portal page:**
- Public route: `/portal/:token` — no auth wall
- Shows: deal title, stage indicator, amount, description
- Timeline of shared activities/notes
- Contact us footer with org name + contact info
- Clean, minimal, branded (org logo if set)

### Exit criteria
- Sales reps can generate and share portal links from deal pages
- External clients can view shared deal info without a CRM account
- Expired/revoked links 404 cleanly
- QA subtask created when done

title: Phase 8 / Saved Searches + Views: frontend UI (view manager, pin bar, filter persistence)

description:
## Context

Tyr has completed the backend API keys infrastructure (OMN-347, CTO-approved). The frontend settings UI is needed to allow admins to create, list, and revoke API keys.

## Task

Build the API key management page in the Settings section.

### Requirements (from roadmap Phase 9 Area 2)

1. **List view** — show all org API keys: name, prefix (e.g. `omn_abc12345...`), scopes, `last_used_at`, created date
2. **Create modal** — form with key name + scope selector (`read` or `write`). On submit:
   - Display plaintext key once in a copy modal (show once, never again)
   - Add to list immediately
3. **Revoke action** — confirm dialog, then DELETE. Remove from list on success.

### API endpoints (already built by Tyr in OMN-347)

- `POST /api/v1/api-keys` — `{ name, scopes }` → returns `{ id, prefix, plaintext_key, ... }` (plaintext once only)
- `GET /api/v1/api-keys` — list for org, no hashes/plaintexts
- `DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/:id` — revoke

### Key decisions
- Admin-only access (mirror backend enforcement)
- Plaintext shown in a dedicated copy modal — cannot be retrieved again
- Format: `omn_<base64url>` — display prefix only in list

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admin can create a named API key with `read` or `write` scope
- Plaintext is shown once and is copyable

title: fix(email): switch renderText to text/template (follow-up from OMN-212)
description:
In `api/internal/email/templates.go`, the `renderText()` function uses `strings.ReplaceAll` for `{{.Key}}` substitution instead of `text/template`. The HTML variant already uses `html/template` correctly.

Risk: a ticket subject or body containing the literal string `{{.` would produce garbled output in the plaintext email part.

Fix: replace the `renderText` helper with a proper `text/template` parse+execute, matching the pattern used by `renderHTML`.

This is a non-breaking quality fix — no schema or API changes required.

title: Test issue creation
Wrap leads convert endpoint in a DB transaction (OMN-134 follow-up)
description:
## Context

Flagged during CTO review of OMN-134.

## Problem

`POST /api/v1/leads/:id/convert` currently makes two separate DB calls:
1. `contacts.Create()` — INSERT into contacts
2. `leads.ConvertToContact()` — UPDATE leads SET status=converted, converted_contact_id=...

If call #2 fails, an orphaned contact row is left with no lead referencing it.

## Required Fix

Wrap both writes in a single database transaction so they succeed or fail together. This requires:
- Passing a `pgx.Tx` through the operation or adding a `ConvertWithTx` method to `LeadRepo`/`ContactRepo`
- The handler initiates the transaction; both repo calls use it

## Priority

Low — convert is a low-frequency path and orphaned contacts are easy to detect and clean up. Fix before next major release.
